messages.content: I'm planning a trip to Munich and need to check the weather for this Sunday. Can you retrieve the weather forecast for Munich?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to retrieve weather forecast for Munich for this Sunday. We have a function to call: requests_get. We need to provide URL, headers, params. The Open-Meteo API endpoint: likely "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need latitude and longitude for Munich. Munich coordinates: approx 48.1351° N, 11.5820° E. So latitude=48.1351, longitude=11.5820. We want forecast for this Sunday. We need to specify daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, etc. Also need to specify timezone. For Sunday, we need to get date. Today is 2026-06-22. Sunday after that? Let's compute: 2026-06-22 is a Thursday? Let's check: 2026-06-22. We can approximate: 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Actually 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Let's quickly compute: 2025-01-01 was a Wednesday? Wait, 2025-01-01 is a Wednesday? Let's check known: 2024-01-01 is Monday. 2025-01-01 is Wednesday (since 2024 is leap year, 366 days, so +2 days). 2026-01-01 is Thursday (since 2025 is not leap, 365 days, +1 day). So 2026-01-01 is Thursday. Then 2026-06-22: from Jan 1 to June 22: Jan 31 days, Feb 28 (2026 not leap), Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 22 days. Sum: 31+28+31+30+31+22 = 173 days. 173 mod 7 = 173 - 7*24=173-168=5. So 2026-06-22 is Thursday +5 days = Tuesday? Wait, starting from Jan 1 Thursday, add 173 days: 173 mod 7 = 5, so day of week = Thursday +5 = Tuesday. So 2026-06-22 is Tuesday. So Sunday after that is 2026-06-25. So we need forecast for 2026-06-25. We can request daily forecast for that date. The Open-Meteo API supports daily parameters and start_date, end_date. So we can set start_date=2026-06-25, end_date=2026-06-25. Provide daily parameters: temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, windgusts_10m_max, etc. But we just need general forecast. We'll request daily: temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, windspeed_10m_max. Provide timezone=Europe/Berlin. So the request: GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=48.1351&longitude=11.5820&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,windspeed_10m_max&start_date=2026-06-25&end_date=2026-06-25&timezone=Europe/Berlin.

We need to call the function.
